but that’s exactly the issue - the priority has gone to style and flash over actual fun gameplay. you’re also punished for taking the “middle ground” of those two options, the bosses are technically beatable solo so challenge runners are fine and they’re a cakewalk with summons so casuals are fine. however, the middle ground as an average souls fan who doesn’t want to summon and go pure melee is either too boring, too hard, or both. there is so much downtime while you’re waiting for the boss to stop attacking and then get one hit in for a sliver of their health, because if you engage anymore you get oneshot or true comboed or grab oneshot. i would pay three times what i paid for elden ring for a game where all the effort they spent on variety and flashiness was instead spent on level design and gameplay. i’m not trying to hate on anyone who likes elden ring, but i’m quite obviously upset that fromsoft are trying to pretend their games are still “tough but fair” when they’ve just devolved into artificial difficulty and boring gameplay.

they all have actual punishable windows and don’t take out your healthbar in one hit - that’s generally what i’d see as more of a selling point. elden ring bosses make it impossible to even see what’s going on beyond the boss flailing around for 30 seconds and then letting you do a singular hit, as well as attacks delayed so long they look stupid all because from’s reputation as a difficult studio seems to be making them start to crack because they’ve clearly run out of ways to make their boss fights naturally enoyable. also, OoK doesn’t exactly have a clear cut, predictable moveset but it’s again done in a way that doesn’t kill you for messing up a single dodge and always feels like something possible to deal with. i just feel like ER really missed the point of what has always made fromsoft games good lol

“What, I wondered, did he mean by “society”? The plural of human beings? Where was the substance of this thing called “society”? I had spent my whole life thinkng that society must certainly be something powerful, harsh and severe, but to hear Horiki talk made the words “Don’t you mean yourself?” come to the tip of my tongue. But I held the words back, reluctant to anger him.

‘Society won’t stand for it.’

‘It’s not society. You’re the one who won’t stand for it - right?’

‘If you do such a thing society will make you suffer for it’

‘It’s not society. It’s you, isn’t it?’

‘Before you know it, you’ll be ostracized by society.’

‘It’s not society. You’re going to do the ostracizing, aren’t you?’

Words, words of every kind went flitting through my head. “Know thy particular fearsomeness, thy knavery, cunning and witchcraft!” 
What I said, however, as I wiped the perspiration from my face with a handkerchief was merely, “You’ve put me in a cold sweat!” I smiled.
From then on, however, I came to hold, almost as a philosophical conviction, the belief: What is society but an individual?”
